museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Republic of Singapore Air Force Super Skyhawk number 928, probably originally A-4C BuNo 147797 c/n 12561, which served with USMC squadrons VMA-343, VMA-223, VMA-211 and VMA-214 and later the US Navy. Dismantled at Cazaux in December 2009 and delivered on 8 January 2010.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Number 1047, radio callsign Pélican 47, left the factory on 1 May 1976 as the twelfth and last for the Sécurité Civile; accident on 30 September 1978 while scooping off Mandelieu. Dismantled at Marignane in November 2004 and trucked to Mérignac in January 2005.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: The first production Falcon 20, first flown 1 January 1965; used for type certification, then Air France crew training and converted into a six-degrees-of-freedom variable-stability simulator, in which configuration it never flew. Retired 1988 with 6248 hours; bought from the Domaines by the conservatory.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Crusader number 32 in flottille 12F colours, one of 17 upgraded between 1994 and 1996; last flight 22 September 1999 with 5389 hours and 1086 deck landings. Dismantled at Landivisiau in May-June 2006 and trucked to Bordeaux-Mérignac.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Mirage IIIC number 2, first flown 13 December 1960; delivered to the CEAM at Mont-de-Marsan on 20 January 1961 as F-SDAA, repaired at Mérignac after a 1961 landing accident, then the CEV at Istres as F-ZADY until January 1991.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Mirage IIIE number 560, delivered new to the CEV at Istres on 14 March 1969 for weapon trials, in particular the AN 52 nuclear bomb. Fitted with a Mirage IIIR nose and camera fairings in place of the Cyrano radar and Doppler.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Noratlas number 188, taken on charge 19 January 1960 by CIET 340 at Toulouse as 340-HB; repaired 1963 after an accident, then ET III/62 Sahara (62-SB), ET II/63 Bigorre (63-BU), converted to flying-classroom standard 1968-1969 and used by GE 316 (316-FS) and ET I/63.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Super Frelon number 165, first flown 31 July 1974 and delivered to the Navy on 25 September 1974; flottille 32F at Lanvéoc-Poulmic from 1977 and flottille 20S at Saint-Raphaël from 1979. Flew in to the conservatory on 5 May 2010.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Full-scale reproduction of Guynemer's SPAD VII, built in 1989 from original drawings for an Armée de l'Air reception at Dakar-Ouakam using steel tube, wood and tarpaulin; the association describes it as a display reproduction rather than a faithful replica.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: The second Jaguar prototype, first flown 11 February 1969 by Bernard Witt; used for air-conditioning, flutter, engine and two-seat spinning trials. Later toured with the Air Force public-relations exhibition in desert camouflage carrying the false number E1.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Mystère IVA number 299, first flown at Mérignac 26 November 1956 and assigned to the Patrouille de France on 14 January 1957 as F-UGEY within EC 3/2 Alsace at Dijon; later F-UGFK with the 7e escadre at Nancy and F-UGCH with EC 3/7 Languedoc.
museum_name: Conservatoire de l'Air et de l'Espace d'Aquitaine

description: Construction number 29138, one of 155 A-26C-50-DT delivered to the USAAF on 19 June 1945; later B-26C, TB-26C, TB-26B and RB-26C with US training and materiel units before coming to Europe. Restored by the conservatory over 17 years.
